source_row.rationale: Trigeminal neuralgia is characterized by sudden, severe, brief episodes of stabbing or electric shock-like facial pain along the distribution of the trigeminal nerve, often triggered by routine activities such as chewing, talking, or light touch, distinct from the more prolonged, throbbing pain typical of migraine.
source_row.source_detail: Clinical presentation: sudden brief electric-shock-like facial pain triggered by benign stimuli; 2025 review, accessed 2026-08-14.
